As John Ternus' era begins, Apple's leadership is also seeing more changes. According to a new report from Bloomberg today, Apple has appointed a new head of mergers and acquisitions, as well as a new vice president of the App Store.

9to5Mac is sponsored by Sony: Sony's premium BRAVIA TVs are seeing significant price cuts, from entry-level models to flagship products—shop now and enjoy the deals!

According to the report, Apple has appointed Steve Smith as the new head of mergers and acquisitions. Smith succeeds Adrian Perica, who joined Apple in 2009 and led the mergers and acquisitions and corporate development team for over a decade. Bloomberg describes Smith as Perica's "long-time deputy" and reports that he will report to CFO Kevan Parekh.

Meanwhile, Perica will take on a "more prominent role" in Apple's Services division. He has been responsible for iCloud, Fitness+, and Apple News since 2023, and will now report directly to Services chief Eddy Cue.

In fact, both Perica and Apple Music head Oliver Schusser are seen as potential successors to Cue.

Additionally, Bloomberg also mentioned today that Apple is promoting Carson Oliver to vice president of the App Store, reporting to Cue. The App Store was previously overseen by Apple Fellow Phil Schiller, until his retirement in August.
